# Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits — facts

## How it works

- [statement] Validate fixture inputs as well as policies. Schema-aware request construction checks principal/action/resource/context compatibility; schema-based JSON parsing checks entity attributes and context shape. Cedar documents CLI and Rust Request::new() utilities, and cedarpy Entities.from_json_str accepts an optional schema. CLI 3.0.0 introduced request validation by default when a schema is supplied, with an explicit option to disable it. (medium confidence) — https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits · also: https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar/blob/main/cedar-policy-cli/CHANGELOG.md, https://github.com/k9securityio/cedar-py
- [statement] When the locally assumed schema changes, revalidate policies and rebuild or recheck request/entity fixtures. Cedar documents that previously valid policies can become invalid after a schema change; independently checking entity construction against the new schema helps expose fixture drift. (medium confidence) — https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits · also: https://github.com/k9securityio/cedar-py

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Do not copy corpus-test leniency into a policy regression gate without review: cedar-py documents soft-passing policy/schema parse failures when a corpus fixture expects Deny. A stricter application gate should fail parse errors separately rather than treating them as successful negative tests. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://github.com/k9securityio/cedar-py · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Parsing and schema validation catch different defects: syntactically valid entity/action misspellings or invalid operand types can survive parsing. The independent cedar-py binding exposes PolicySet.from_str for parsing and validate_policies(policies, schema), returning validation_passed, for checking a supplied schema. These local checks do not establish Atlas compatibility. (medium confidence) — https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/automate-cedar-policy-validation-with-aws-developer-tools/, https://github.com/k9securityio/cedar-py
- [statement] An author-supplied schema lets local validation check declared entity types, actions, action-specific principal/resource types, context shapes, attribute names, and operator types. These checks test consistency with that supplied model. (medium confidence) — https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits · also: https://github.com/k9securityio/cedar-py
- [statement] The upstream fixture harness separates `cedar validate --policies policies.cedar --schema schema.cedarschema --schema-format cedar` from `cedar authorize --policies policies.cedar --schema schema.cedarschema --schema-format cedar --entities entities.json --request-json request.json -v`; the two gates check different properties. (medium confidence) — https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar-examples/blob/release/4.12.x/test_utils.sh · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/automate-cedar-policy-validation-with-aws-developer-tools/, https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html
- [statement] Keep request JSON, entity data and expected outcomes together and rerun positive and negative cases after edits. The upstream harness iterates ALLOW/*.json and DENY/*.json, invokes cedar authorize with optional schema, and compares actual decisions. AWS demonstrates a changed policy failing an expected-outcome test; cedarpy also exposes decision assertions and diagnostics. These are local scenario regressions, not Atlas conformance tests. (medium confidence) — https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/automate-cedar-policy-validation-with-aws-developer-tools/ · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits · also: https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar-examples/blob/release/4.12.x/test_utils.sh, https://github.com/k9securityio/cedar-py
- [statement] For Atlas, treat a schema reconstructed from documented actions and context examples as an author-maintained approximation. Local success does not replace submitting policy bodies to Atlas validation or checking behavior in the non-production organization and fresh cluster recommended by MongoDB. The reviewed material does not establish an authoritative downloadable Atlas schema or a local conformance contract. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies.md · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/opensource/decoupling-authorization-at-scale-mongodb-atlas-and-cedar-based-resource-policies/, https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/policies/validation.html
- [statement] A concrete implementation-parity counterexample was reported for cedar-go experimental strict validation: an October 17, 2026 reproduction on main b1be45e accepted undeclared enum entity IDs in policy scope that Rust cedar-policy 4.13.0 rejected. Record engine/build details with fixtures; this report is not evidence about Atlas and does not establish the current fix status. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-17) — https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar-go/issues/163 · keywords: Local Cedar schema and request-fixture tests with Atlas parity limits
